clue.text: Author is writer of particular kind of verse

blocks.note: the author of the clue speaking of themself: 'I am'
a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a writing tool

explanation.surface: A poet who specialises in one particular verse form.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords often use 'author' or 'setter' for the person who wrote the clue, so 'Author is' becomes I AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambic describes poetry built from iambs, metrical feet of one unstressed then one stressed syllable.

clue.text: College backed up reserve computer

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top, the other way round

blocks.note: Eton College, the English public school
to book is to reserve, as with a table

explanation.surface: A college has backed up its files on a spare computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed up' and 'reserve' read like IT jargon about backups, but one turns a school round and the other means book.
explanation.definitionFit: A notebook is a small portable laptop machine, so it is a kind of personal computing device.

clue.text: Novel alibi could be immune to challenge

indicators.note: 'could be' suggests the letters might be rearranged into something else entirely

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A suspect's original excuse might stand up to any cross-examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; 'could be' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inviolable cannot be broken, attacked or infringed, so it stands beyond any dispute or assault.

clue.text: Stepped right over naked body

indicators.note: turned over, so the abbreviation for right is read backwards
stripped naked means its outer covering is taken away, leaving the inside of the word

blocks.note: RT is a standard abbreviation of right
the word body with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone walked straight over a nude corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: Trod is the past tense of tread, meaning walked or put a foot down on something.

clue.text: Carry on deregulating banks over there

indicators.note: to bank is to hold or keep, so the phrase holds the letters within it
removing the rules lets the captured letters fall out of their set order

blocks.note: the letters running across the end of carry, all of on and the start of deregulating

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep freeing the banking sector from regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters RYONDE sit inside 'carRY ON DEregulating' and are then rearranged into YONDER; 'deregulating' serves twice, holding letters and signalling the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old-fashioned adverb pointing to a place some distance away, within sight.

clue.text: University lecturer buried in vault with separate compartments

indicators.note: something buried in a place is inside it, enclosed by it

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
L is the abbreviation for lecturer
a cellar is an underground vault

explanation.surface: An academic has been entombed in a crypt divided into chambers.
explanation.walkthrough: The two abbreviations go inside after the CELL of CELLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellular means made up of many cells, small separate units or chambers, as in cellular blankets or structures.

clue.text: Gondola, out of its depth, capsized in lake

indicators.note: read literally, the abbreviation for depth is out of the boat's name, so that letter goes
a capsized boat is tipped over, so its letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for depth, removed

explanation.surface: A Venetian boat, out of its element, overturns in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Venice really has a lagoon full of gondolas, so the surface sits right inside the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of salt water cut off from the sea, a shallow coastal lake.

clue.text: Way of working on part of test in addition

blocks.note: MO, modus operandi, a way of working
re means on or concerning
an over is a set of six balls in a Test (cricket) match

explanation.surface: A method of tackling a section of an exam, offered as an extra.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, played in overs of six deliveries each.
explanation.definitionFit: Moreover is a sentence adverb introducing a further point, meaning besides or furthermore.

clue.text: After outlying event, this essentially sees arid remnant transformed

definitions.text: After outlying event, this essentially sees arid remnant transformed

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its inner letters are kept
transformed means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the two inner letters of sees
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A geological catastrophe left this sea a dry relic.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: about six million years ago, cut off from the Atlantic, the sea almost dried out (the Messinian salinity crisis).
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists record that the Mediterranean sea evaporated when its Atlantic link closed, leaving salt flats and basins.

clue.text: In possession of intelligence American leaked about men I'd compromised

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps round the other
compromised means weakened or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
leaked out like a dye that runs
the letters of men and I'd, rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy story: an American with secret information leaks it, compromising agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' and 'leaked' paint espionage; the definition uses intelligence in its plain sense of brainpower.
explanation.definitionFit: Able-minded means having a capable, competent mind, so such a person has plenty of brains.

clue.text: Controversial artist scandalised crowds

indicators.note: to crowd something is to press around it, so the word encloses the letters

blocks.note: the letters sitting in the middle of scandalised

explanation.surface: A provocative painter shocks his audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí, the Spanish surrealist, courted outrage with his flamboyant persona and provocative paintings.

clue.text: Train group of swimmers

blocks.note: first meaning: to teach or educate
second meaning: a large shoal of fish

explanation.surface: A coach drilling a swimming squad.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to teach or discipline; as a noun it names a shoal of fish or whales.

clue.text: Runners enlist doctor after training

indicators.note: after training the letters are put into a new shape, as a trainee is reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: Athletes sign up a medic once their training is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests athletes, but here it means plant shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendrils are slender climbing shoots that creep along and twine, like the runners of a plant.

clue.text: Controlling regime votes against accepting new head of National Gallery

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one word goes inside another
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: nays are votes cast against a motion
N is the abbreviation for new
the opening letter of National
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Opposition to the appointment of a new director at an art museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a London art gallery; 'National Gallery' looks like one name but splits across two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny state is a government seen as overprotective, interfering in private choices like a strict childminder.

clue.text: Singer's last to join rescue vessel

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only

blocks.note: the final letter of join
Noah's Ark rescued the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: A singer's final job is to board a lifeboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer's last' looks like the letter R, but 'Singer' is the definition: to sing is slang for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A nark is British slang for a police informer, someone who sings, that is, betrays others.

clue.text: Henry abandons anguished unorthodox Christian figure

indicators.note: whatever abandons a word leaves it, so that letter is removed
unorthodox means not following the usual pattern, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A distressed, heterodox believer is deserted by Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnus Dei, Latin for Lamb of God, is an emblem of Christ shown as a lamb bearing a cross.

clue.text: Reporter's incapable of producing issue for boss?

indicators.note: a reporter's version is a spoken account, so the word is heard rather than read

blocks.note: barren means unable to have children, issue being offspring

explanation.surface: A journalist reports that the boss is infertile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' suggests a newspaper edition, but here means children.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a powerful magnate controlling an industry, such as a press baron, hence a boss; the question mark flags the loose sense.

clue.text: Airs broadcast showing coverage of Indian women

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Television programmes that report on women in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coverage' looks like media reporting, but it means a garment that covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is a long length of cloth draped around the body, the traditional dress of South Asian women.

clue.text: Member of 11 nicking side of face with blade in the morning

indicators.note: one side of a word is an end, here its final letter
nicking means pinching or taking, so the blade takes the letter inside it

blocks.note: a sabre is a curved sword
the final letter of face
a.m., before noon

explanation.surface: A team member cuts his cheek shaving with a razor one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 across is SCHOOL in its sense of a shoal of fish, so a member is a fish; '11' suggests a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea bream are marine food fish that swim in shoals, so one is a single fish within such a group.

clue.text: Curse three different articles by old lady

blocks.note: the indefinite articles an and a, and the definite article the
ma is an informal word for mother, one's old lady

explanation.surface: Mum swears at three separate newspaper pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: English has three articles, a, an and the; here they are set down as an, a, the.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal ecclesiastical ban or a detested thing, and also an imprecation or malediction.

clue.text: Turbulent state revolutionised dated model

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: if you saw someone, you dated them
to sit for an artist is to model

explanation.surface: An unsettled country rebelled against an outdated pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiswas is British slang for a state of confusion, also the name of a chaotic 1970s children's TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiswas is informal British slang for a flustered, agitated condition, much like a tizzy.

clue.text: Lady wanting boy makes wishes

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word loses those letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a lad is a boy, removed from the front of lady
to earn money is to make it

explanation.surface: A woman longing for a son.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Lady wanting boy' as a woman yearning for a son; really the definition is 'wishes', a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long or desire something intensely, the verb sense matching the third-person form here.

clue.text: Sister finally separating expert's head from body shows subtlety

indicators.note: the sister's word is split just before its end, so something is inserted at that point
the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a nun is a religious sister
an expert is an ace; its first letter
the rest of ace once its head is gone

explanation.surface: A nun beheads a specialist, the act revealing a delicate touch.
explanation.walkthrough: Ace's head goes inside the nun before her last letter, and the headless body of ace follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a fine shade of difference in meaning, colour or tone, hence a subtle distinction.

clue.text: Worshipped woman with two lives

blocks.note: lives means is (exists), and two of them sit side by side

explanation.surface: A woman with a double life who is adored.
explanation.walkthrough: Isis is also the name of the River Thames at Oxford, but here she is the goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was the Egyptian mother goddess, venerated across the ancient world as a deity.

clue.text: Informer taped other suspect

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or not genuine, so the letters are doctored into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A whistleblower secretly recorded another suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep Throat was the codename of the secret source in the Watergate scandal, so it means a leaker of secrets.

clue.text: Platform said to have upset extremists

indicators.note: upsetting the extremes disturbs only the outer letters, so the first and last change places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A podium reportedly provoked radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the end letters S and D swap; the middle AI stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised stage at one end of a hall, where speakers stand.

clue.text: Converse for example with people outside

indicators.note: the people are on the outside, wrapped around the abbreviation

blocks.note: e.g., exempli gratia
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Talking with crowds out of doors, say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converse' looks like a verb meaning chat; it is the noun meaning opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A negation is the opposite or contradiction of a statement, which is what a converse means in logic.

clue.text: Prime minister cutting head of state's hair

indicators.note: cutting a word trims something off it, here from its end

blocks.note: Margaret Thatcher, UK Prime Minister 1979-90
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The PM gives the monarch a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, who was the UK head of state during Thatcher's time.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is an informal term for a thick, untidy mop of hair, likened to a straw roof.
